problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.description: You're given an integer array nums. Return true if some value shows up at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.
problems.hint: A HashSet remembers what you've already seen. What should happen when add() finds the value is already there?

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description: Two strings are anagrams if one can be rearranged into the other using every letter exactly once. Given s and t, return true if they are anagrams of each other.
problems.hint: Count how many times each of the 26 letters appears. Increment for s, decrement for t — what should the counts be at the end?

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array nums and an integer target, find the two different indices whose values add up to target. Return them as [i, j] with i < j.

Every input has exactly one valid answer.
problems.hint: For each number x, the partner you need is target − x. A HashMap from value to index lets you check in O(1) whether that partner appeared earlier.

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.description: The majority element of an array of length n is the value that appears more than n / 2 times. Given nums, return its majority element. One is guaranteed to exist.
problems.hint: Counting with a HashMap works. For O(1) memory: keep a candidate and a counter — matching values add 1, others subtract 1, and a counter of 0 means pick a new candidate.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.description: An array nums holds n distinct numbers taken from the range 0..n (that range has n + 1 values). Exactly one value of the range is missing — return it.
problems.hint: You know what 0 + 1 + … + n adds up to. Compare it with the actual sum of the array.

tests.explain: n = 3, so the range is 0..3. 2 is the one not in the array.

problems.title: Single Number
problems.description:
In the array nums, every value appears exactly twice except for one value that appears once. Find that lonely value.

Bonus: can you do it in O(n) time and O(1) extra memory?
problems.hint: A HashSet you add to and remove from works. For O(1) memory, think about XOR: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.description:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after turning uppercase letters into lowercase and throwing away everything that isn't a letter or digit, it reads the same forwards and backwards.

Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome.
problems.hint: Put one pointer at each end. Skip characters that aren't letters/digits (Character.isLetterOrDigit), compare lowercase versions, and move inward.

input: Was it a car or a cat I saw?

tests.explain: Nothing is left after cleaning, and an empty string reads the same both ways.

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.description:
You have two arrays sorted in non-decreasing order: nums1 with m real values followed by n zeros (empty slots), and nums2 with n values.

Merge nums2 into nums1 in place so that nums1 ends up fully sorted. The method returns nothing — the tests check nums1 afterwards.
problems.hint: Fill nums1 from the back: compare the largest remaining values of both arrays and write the bigger one at the end.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.description: Given an array nums, move every 0 to the end while keeping the relative order of the non-zero values. Do it in place — the tests check nums after your method runs.
problems.hint: Keep a 'write' pointer for where the next non-zero value should go. After copying all non-zeros forward, fill the rest with zeros.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description: prices[i] is a stock's price on day i. You may buy on one day and sell on a later day. Return the biggest profit you can make, or 0 if no profit is possible.
problems.hint: Walk through the days keeping the cheapest price seen so far. Selling today earns price − cheapest.

problems.title: Maximum Average Subarray
problems.description:
Given nums and an integer k, find the contiguous block of exactly k elements with the largest average and return that average.

Answers within 10⁻⁵ of the correct value are accepted.
problems.hint: Compute the sum of the first k elements, then slide: add the element entering the window and subtract the one leaving.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description:
The string s contains only the characters ( ) { } [ ]. It is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets close in the correct order.

Return true if s is valid.
problems.hint: Push opening brackets on a stack. A closing bracket must match the top of the stack. What must the stack look like at the end?

problems.title: Baseball Game
problems.description:
You keep score for a strange game. Each entry of ops is one of:

  • an integer x — record a new score of x
  • "+" — record the sum of the previous two scores
  • "D" — record double the previous score
  • "C" — cancel (remove) the previous score

Return the sum of all scores still recorded at the end. Every operation is guaranteed to be valid.
problems.hint: A stack of scores fits perfectly: each operation only looks at (or removes) the most recent entries.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description:
nums is sorted in ascending order with distinct values. Return the index of target, or -1 if it isn't there.

Your solution must run in O(log n).
problems.hint: Look at the middle element. If it's too small, the answer can only be to its right; if too big, to its left. Repeat on the remaining half.

problems.title: Search Insert Position
problems.description:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target, return the index of target if it's present. Otherwise, return the index where it would be inserted to keep the array sorted.

Aim for O(log n).
problems.hint: Binary search for the first index whose value is ≥ target. If no such index exists, the answer is nums.length.

problems.title: Integer Square Root
problems.description:
Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer.

Don't use Math.sqrt or Math.pow — search for the answer instead.
problems.hint: Binary search on the answer r in [0, x]: is r × r ≤ x? Use long for r × r to avoid overflow.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.description:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Walk the list keeping three references: prev, current and next. Point current.next back at prev, then step forward.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.description:
You get the heads of two sorted linked lists, list1 and list2. Splice their nodes together into one sorted list and return its head.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: A dummy head node removes the special case for the first node. Repeatedly attach the smaller of the two current nodes.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.description:
Given the head of a linked list, return true if the list contains a cycle — some node can be reached again by following next pointers.

Challenge: use O(1) memory.

Test input: the node values, plus pos = the index the tail connects back to (−1 means no cycle). pos is not passed to your method.
problems.hint: Floyd's tortoise and hare: move one pointer 1 step and another 2 steps at a time. If there's a cycle, they must meet.

problems.title: Middle of the Linked List
problems.description:
Return the middle node of a non-empty singly linked list. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one. (The tests show the list from that node to the end.)

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Move a slow pointer one step and a fast pointer two steps. When fast reaches the end, slow is in the middle.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.description:
Mirror a binary tree: swap the left and right child of every node. Return the root.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Recursion: invert the left subtree, invert the right subtree, then swap them.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description:
Return the depth of a binary tree: the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf. An empty tree has depth 0.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)), and depth(null) = 0.

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.description:
Given the roots p and q of two binary trees, return true if they have exactly the same shape and the same values in the same places.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Two trees are equal if their roots match AND their left subtrees are equal AND their right subtrees are equal. Handle null carefully.

problems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problems.description:
The diameter of a binary tree is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes. The path doesn't have to pass through the root. Return the diameter.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: While computing each node's height, the longest path through that node is height(left) + height(right). Track the max in a field.

tests.explain: The longest path 5 → 3 → 2 → 4 → 6 doesn't use the root.

problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
problems.description:
A binary tree is height-balanced if, at every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most 1. Return true if the tree is balanced.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Compute heights bottom-up and return a special value (like −1) as soon as any subtree is unbalanced, so you don't recompute.

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.description:
Return true if subRoot appears inside root as a complete subtree: some node of root together with all of its descendants has exactly the same structure and values as subRoot.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: For each node of root, check whether the tree starting there is the same tree as subRoot (reuse your 'Same Tree' logic).

tests.explain: Node 4 in root has an extra descendant (0).

problems.title: Longest Common Prefix
problems.description:
Return the longest string that is a prefix of every word in strs. If they share no prefix, return "".

This is a great warm-up for tries: the common prefix is the path from the root while each node has exactly one child.
problems.hint: Compare characters column by column across all words, stopping at the first mismatch or the end of the shortest word.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
problems.description:
Implement class KthLargest that keeps track of the k-th largest value in a growing stream of numbers:

  • KthLargest(int k, int[] nums) starts with the values in nums
  • int add(int val) adds val and returns the current k-th largest value

When add is called, there are always at least k values.

Tests list the calls made and the value each one returns (null for the constructor).
problems.hint: A min-heap (PriorityQueue) that never holds more than k values: its smallest element (peek) is the k-th largest overall.

problems.title: Last Stone Weight
problems.description:
Each turn, take the two heaviest stones and smash them together. If their weights are equal, both are destroyed; otherwise the lighter one is destroyed and the heavier one's weight becomes the difference.

When at most one stone remains, return its weight (or 0 if none remain).
problems.hint: A max-heap gives you the two heaviest stones each turn: new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder()).

problems.title: Flood Fill
problems.description: An image is a grid of integers (pixel colours). Starting from pixel (sr, sc), repaint it and every pixel connected to it 4-directionally (up, down, left, right) that has the same original colour, using color. Return the modified image.
problems.hint: DFS or BFS from the start pixel, only stepping onto neighbours with the original colour. If the new colour equals the original, there's nothing to do (and no infinite loop!).

problems.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
problems.description: An undirected graph has n vertices labelled 0 to n − 1. Each edges[i] = [u, v] connects u and v. Return true if there is a path from source to destination.
problems.hint: Build an adjacency list, then BFS/DFS from source with a visited array. (Union-Find also works.)

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: A staircase has n steps. Each move you climb either 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?
problems.hint: To stand on step n you came from step n − 1 or step n − 2, so ways(n) = ways(n − 1) + ways(n − 2).

problems.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
problems.description: cost[i] is the price of stepping on stair i. After paying, you can climb one or two stairs. You may start on stair 0 or stair 1, and the goal is to get past the last stair. Return the minimum total cost.
problems.hint: Let best[i] be the cheapest way to stand on stair i. best[i] = cost[i] + min(best[i − 1], best[i − 2]); the answer is min of the last two.

problems.title: Counting Bits
problems.description:
Given n, return an array ans of length n + 1 where ans[i] is the number of 1 bits in the binary form of i.

Challenge: O(n) without a built-in bit counter.
problems.hint: i >> 1 drops the last bit, and you've already computed it: ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1).

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.description:
Given an array of lowercase words strs, put words that are anagrams of each other into the same group. Return the list of groups.

Groups, and the words inside each group, may be in any order.
problems.hint: Anagrams share a 'signature': the sorted letters, or the 26 letter counts. Use that signature as a HashMap key.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k values that occur most often, in any order.

The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
problems.hint: Count frequencies with a HashMap. Then either sort by count, use a min-heap of size k, or bucket values by their frequency (O(n)).

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.description:
Given nums, build an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i].

Do it in O(n) time without using division.
constraints: All products fit in a 32-bit int
problems.hint: answer[i] = (product of everything to the left of i) × (product of everything to the right of i). Two passes, one in each direction.

problems.title: Valid Sudoku
problems.description:
A 9×9 Sudoku board is given as a grid of characters: digits '1'–'9' or '.' for an empty cell. The board is valid if no digit repeats inside any row, any column, or any of the nine 3×3 boxes.

Only the filled cells need to be checked — the board doesn't have to be solvable.
problems.hint: Use 27 sets (9 rows, 9 columns, 9 boxes). The box of cell (r, c) is (r / 3) * 3 + c / 3.

tests.explain: Column 0 has two 8s (and so does the top-left box).
Both 2s sit in the top-left 3×3 box.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.description:
Given an unsorted array nums, return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers (like 4, 5, 6, 7) that can be formed from its values. Order in the array doesn't matter.

Aim for O(n) time.
problems.hint: Put everything in a HashSet. Only start counting from x if x − 1 is NOT in the set — that way each run is counted once.

problems.title: Two Sum II – Sorted Input
problems.description:
numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order. Find two numbers that add up to target and return their positions 1-indexed, as [index1, index2] with index1 < index2.

Exactly one solution exists. Use only O(1) extra memory.
problems.hint: Start with pointers at both ends. If the sum is too small, which pointer should move to make it bigger?

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.description:
Given nums, return every unique triplet [a, b, c] of values taken from three different positions such that a + b + c == 0.

The same triplet of values must not appear twice. Triplets (and the numbers inside them) may be returned in any order.
problems.hint: Sort first. Fix the first number, then use two pointers on the rest of the array to find pairs summing to its negative. Skip equal neighbours to avoid duplicates.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.description:
height[i] is the height of a vertical wall standing at position i. Pick two walls; together with the ground they form a container holding min(height[i], height[j]) × (j − i) units of water.

Return the maximum amount of water any pair can hold.
problems.hint: Start with the widest container (both ends). The shorter wall limits the water, so moving the taller one inward can never help — move the shorter one.

problems.title: Sort Colors
problems.description:
nums contains only 0s, 1s and 2s (think red, white, blue). Sort it in place so all 0s come first, then 1s, then 2s — without calling a library sort.

Challenge: one pass, O(1) memory.
problems.hint: Dutch national flag: keep three pointers — low (next spot for 0), mid (current), high (next spot for 2). Swap and move depending on nums[mid].

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring (contiguous piece) in which no character appears twice.
constraints: s has letters, digits, symbols and spaces
problems.hint: Grow a window to the right. When the new character is already inside the window, shrink from the left until it isn't. A map of last-seen positions lets you jump directly.

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.description: You have a string s of uppercase letters and may change at most k characters into any other uppercase letter. Return the length of the longest substring that can be made of one repeated letter.
problems.hint: A window is fixable if (window length − count of its most frequent letter) ≤ k. Grow right; when it breaks, move left by one.

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.description: Given two lowercase strings s1 and s2, return true if some rearrangement of s1 appears as a contiguous substring of s2.
problems.hint: Slide a window of length s1.length() across s2 and compare 26-letter counts with s1's counts.

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.description:
Design a stack that, besides the usual operations, can return its minimum element in constant time. Implement class MinStack:

  • MinStack() creates an empty stack
  • void push(int val)
  • void pop() removes the top element
  • int top() returns the top element
  • int getMin() returns the smallest element in the stack

All four methods must run in O(1). pop, top and getMin are only called on non-empty stacks.

Tests list the calls made and the value each one returns (null for void methods).
problems.hint: Alongside each value, store the minimum of the stack at the moment it was pushed (a second stack, or pairs).

problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.description:
An arithmetic expression is written in Reverse Polish Notation: operators come after their two operands, e.g. ["2","1","+","3","*"] means (2 + 1) * 3. Evaluate tokens and return the result.

Operators are + - * /; division truncates toward zero (like Java's / on ints). The expression is always valid and never divides by zero.
constraints: Intermediate results fit in an int
problems.hint: Numbers go on a stack. An operator pops two values — careful: the first one popped is the RIGHT operand.

problems.title: Generate Parentheses
problems.description: Given n, return every string of n pairs of parentheses that is well-formed (balanced). Any order is accepted.
problems.hint: Build strings character by character. You may add '(' while you have opens left, and ')' only when it wouldn't close more than you've opened.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.description: temperatures[i] is the temperature on day i. For each day, return how many days you must wait for a strictly warmer day, or 0 if no warmer day comes.
problems.hint: Keep a stack of days still waiting for a warmer day (their temperatures decrease from bottom to top). Today resolves every waiting day that is colder.

problems.title: Car Fleet
problems.description:
n cars drive along a one-lane road toward a destination at mile target. Car i starts at position[i] with constant speed[i]. A car can never pass another: when it catches up, it slows down and they drive together as a fleet.

Catching up exactly at the destination still counts as one fleet. Return how many fleets arrive at the destination.
problems.hint: Sort cars by position, closest to the target first. Compute each car's arrival time; a car that would arrive no later than the fleet in front of it joins that fleet.

problems.title: Search a 2D Matrix
problems.description:
In matrix, each row is sorted ascending, and the first value of each row is greater than the last value of the previous row. Return true if target is in the matrix.

Aim for O(log(m·n)).
problems.hint: Read row by row, the matrix is one sorted list of m·n values. Index k maps to matrix[k / n][k % n].

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.description:
There are piles of bananas, piles[i] in pile i. Koko picks an eating speed k (bananas per hour). Each hour she chooses one pile and eats k bananas from it — if the pile has fewer, she finishes it and waits for the rest of that hour.

Return the smallest k that lets her finish everything within h hours.
problems.hint: If speed k works, every bigger speed works too. Binary search k in [1, max pile]; hours for a pile is ceil(pile / k). Sum hours in a long.

problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.description: An ascending array of distinct values was rotated some number of times (e.g. [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] might become [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]). Return its minimum element in O(log n).
problems.hint: Compare nums[mid] with nums[hi]. If nums[mid] > nums[hi], the minimum is to the right of mid; otherwise it's at mid or to its left.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.description: nums is an ascending array of distinct values that may have been rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of target, or -1 if it isn't present. Required: O(log n).
problems.hint: At every step, at least one half (lo..mid or mid..hi) is sorted. Check whether the target lies inside that sorted half to decide where to go.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.description:
Remove the n-th node counting from the end of the list and return the head. Try to do it in a single pass.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Use a dummy node before head. Move a fast pointer n steps ahead, then move both until fast hits the end — slow is right before the node to delete.

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.description:
A list L0 → L1 → … → Ln-1 → Ln must be rearranged in place into L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln-1 → L2 → Ln-2 → …. Change the links, not the values. The method returns nothing — tests check the list starting at head.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Three steps: find the middle, reverse the second half, then weave the two halves together.

problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.description:
Two non-negative integers are stored as linked lists of digits in reverse order (the head holds the ones digit). Add them and return the sum as a list in the same format.

The numbers have no leading zeros, except the number 0 itself.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Add digit by digit like on paper, carrying when a column reaches 10. Don't forget a final carry.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.description:
Return the values of a binary tree level by level: a list of lists where list d holds the values at depth d, from left to right.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Breadth-first search with a queue. At the start of each round, queue.size() tells you how many nodes belong to the current level.

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.description:
Imagine standing to the right of a binary tree. Return the values of the nodes you can see, from top to bottom (the rightmost node of each level).

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Level-order traversal, keeping only the last node of each level. (Or DFS visiting right before left, recording the first node seen at each depth.)

tests.explain: Node 4 is on the left, but nothing blocks it on its level.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.description:
Return true if the tree is a valid binary search tree: for every node, all values in its left subtree are strictly smaller and all values in its right subtree are strictly larger than the node's value.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: Checking only a node's direct children isn't enough. Pass down an allowed (low, high) range — use long bounds so Integer.MIN/MAX values work.

tests.explain: 3 is in 5's right subtree but is smaller than 5.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.description:
Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, return the k-th smallest value in the tree (1-indexed).

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: An in-order traversal (left, node, right) of a BST visits values in sorted order. Stop at the k-th visit.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
problems.description:
Given a binary search tree and two values p and q that both exist in it, return the value of their lowest common ancestor: the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node counts as a descendant of itself).

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
constraints: All values are unique; p ≠ q
problems.hint: Use the BST ordering: if both values are smaller than the current node, go left; if both are larger, go right; otherwise you've found the split point.

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.description:
A trie stores strings in a tree where each edge is a letter, so words sharing a prefix share a path. Implement class Trie:

  • Trie() creates an empty trie
  • void insert(String word)
  • boolean search(String word) — true if word was inserted
  • boolean startsWith(String prefix) — true if any inserted word starts with prefix

Tests list the calls made and the value each one returns (null for void methods).
problems.hint: Each node has 26 child slots and an 'end of word' flag. search needs the flag at the last node; startsWith only needs the path to exist.

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words
problems.description:
Implement class WordDictionary:

  • WordDictionary() creates an empty dictionary
  • void addWord(String word)
  • boolean search(String word) — true if some added word matches. word may contain dots '.', and a dot matches any one letter.

Tests list the calls made and the value each one returns (null for void methods).
constraints: Lowercase letters; search patterns may include '.'
problems.hint: Store words in a trie. When searching, a dot means 'try every existing child' — a small DFS.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.description:
Return the k-th largest element of nums in sorted order (not the k-th distinct value). For example, the 2nd largest of [3, 3, 1] is 3.

Can you beat sorting the whole array?
problems.hint: Keep a min-heap of size k as you scan — O(n log k). Quickselect is O(n) on average.

problems.title: K Closest Points to Origin
problems.description:
Each points[i] = [x, y] is a point on the plane. Return the k points closest to the origin (0, 0) by Euclidean distance, in any order.

The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
problems.hint: You don't need the square root — compare x² + y². A max-heap of size k (evict the farthest) or sorting both work.

problems.title: Task Scheduler
problems.description:
A CPU must run a list of tasks, each labelled with a capital letter and taking one time unit. In each unit the CPU either runs one task or stays idle. Two runs of the same task must be separated by at least n units.

Return the minimum number of units needed to finish every task.
problems.hint: The most frequent task dictates the shape: (maxCount − 1) blocks of length n + 1, plus one slot per task that ties for the max count. The answer is never less than tasks.length.

tests.explain: A B idle A B idle A B

problems.title: Subsets
problems.description: Given an array of distinct integers, return all possible subsets (the power set), including the empty set. No duplicate subsets; any order is accepted (for the subsets and the values inside them).
problems.hint: For each element there are two choices: include it or not. Recurse through the array making that choice, and record the current subset at every leaf.

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.description:
Given distinct positive candidates and a target, return every unique combination of candidates that adds up to target. The same candidate may be used any number of times.

Two combinations are the same if they use the same numbers the same number of times. Any order is accepted.
problems.hint: Backtrack with a start index: at index i you may take candidates[i] again (stay at i) or move on to i + 1. Never look back, so you don't produce the same combination in two orders.

problems.title: Permutations
problems.description: Given an array of distinct integers, return all of its permutations (every possible ordering). The permutations may be listed in any order.
problems.hint: Build each permutation position by position, marking which values are already used. Undo the choice after the recursive call returns.

problems.title: Subsets II
problems.description: Like Subsets, but nums may contain duplicates. Return all possible subsets without listing the same subset twice. Any order is accepted.
problems.hint: Sort first so equal values sit together. When you decide to skip a value, skip all of its copies too.

problems.title: Word Search
problems.description: Given an m × n grid of letters and a word, return true if the word can be traced through horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, using each cell at most once.
problems.hint: Start a DFS from every cell matching word[0]. Temporarily mark a cell as visited (e.g. replace it with '#') and restore it when backtracking.

tests.explain: The B would have to be reused.

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
problems.description: On an old phone keypad, digits map to letters: 2→abc, 3→def, 4→ghi, 5→jkl, 6→mno, 7→pqrs, 8→tuv, 9→wxyz. Given a string of digits 2-9, return every letter string it could spell, in any order. An empty input gives an empty list.
problems.hint: Recursion over the digits: for each letter of the current digit, append it and recurse on the next digit.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.description: The grid contains '1' (land) and '0' (water). An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically. Return how many islands there are. Everything outside the grid is water.
problems.hint: Scan every cell. When you hit unvisited land, count a new island and sink the whole island with DFS/BFS so you don't count it again.

problems.title: Max Area of Island
problems.description: The grid contains 1 (land) and 0 (water). An island is a group of 1s connected 4-directionally, and its area is its number of cells. Return the largest island area, or 0 if there is no land.
problems.hint: Like Number of Islands, but have your DFS return how many cells it sank.

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.description:
Each cell of the grid is 0 (empty), 1 (fresh orange) or 2 (rotten orange). Every minute, each fresh orange that is 4-directionally next to a rotten one becomes rotten.

Return the minimum number of minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if that never happens.
problems.hint: Multi-source BFS: start with ALL rotten oranges in the queue at minute 0 and expand one layer per minute. Count fresh oranges to know whether any were unreachable.

tests.explain: The bottom-left orange can never be reached.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.description: There are numCourses courses labelled 0 to numCourses − 1. Each prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means you must take course b before course a. Return true if it is possible to finish every course.
problems.hint: It's impossible exactly when the prerequisite graph has a cycle. Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take courses with no remaining prerequisites and count how many you managed to take.

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.description:
heights is an island map. The Pacific touches the top and left edges; the Atlantic touches the bottom and right edges. Rain flows from a cell to a 4-directional neighbour whose height is less than or equal.

Return the coordinates [r, c] of every cell from which water can reach both oceans, in any order.
problems.hint: Reverse the flow: DFS from each ocean's border cells going UPHILL (to neighbours ≥ current). Answer = cells reached from both oceans.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components
problems.description: An undirected graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n − 1 and the given edges. Return the number of connected components (groups of nodes reachable from each other).
problems.hint: Union-Find: start with n components, and every edge that joins two different sets reduces the count by one. (DFS over unvisited nodes also works.)

problems.title: House Robber
problems.description: Houses along a street hold nums[i] money each. You can't rob two adjacent houses (the alarms are linked). Return the maximum amount you can take.
problems.hint: At house i you either skip it (best up to i − 1) or rob it (nums[i] + best up to i − 2). Keep just the last two values.

problems.title: House Robber II
problems.description: Same rules as House Robber, but the houses stand in a circle: the first and the last house are neighbours. Return the maximum amount you can take.
problems.hint: You can't rob both the first and the last house. Run the linear House Robber twice: once without the last house, once without the first.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.description: You have unlimited coins of each value in coins. Return the fewest coins needed to make exactly amount, or -1 if it can't be done.
problems.hint: dp[a] = fewest coins for amount a. dp[0] = 0, and dp[a] = 1 + min over coins c ≤ a of dp[a − c]. Greedy (biggest coin first) does NOT always work.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.description: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums. A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements.
problems.hint: O(n²): len[i] = 1 + max(len[j]) over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]. O(n log n): keep the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search.

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.description: Return the length of the longest subsequence shared by text1 and text2 (characters in the same order, not necessarily contiguous). Return 0 if they share none.
problems.hint: 2-D table: dp[i][j] = LCS of the first i chars and first j chars. Equal chars → dp[i−1][j−1] + 1, otherwise max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1]).

problems.title: Word Break
problems.description: Return true if string s can be split into a sequence of one or more words from wordDict. Dictionary words may be reused.
problems.hint: ok[i] = can the first i characters be split? ok[0] = true; ok[i] is true if some word w ends at i and ok[i − w.length()] is true.

problems.title: First Missing Positive
problems.description:
Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest positive integer (1, 2, 3, …) that does not appear in it.

Your algorithm must run in O(n) time and use O(1) extra memory (you may modify the array).
problems.hint: The answer is always in 1..n+1. Try to place each value v (when 1 ≤ v ≤ n) at index v − 1 by swapping, then scan for the first index whose value is wrong.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.description:
height describes a skyline of bars, each 1 unit wide. After it rains, water collects between taller bars. Return the total number of units of water trapped.

Water above bar i = min(tallest bar to its left, tallest bar to its right) − height[i] (if positive).
problems.hint: Two pointers with running leftMax and rightMax: whichever side has the smaller max is the one whose water level you already know for sure.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.description:
Given strings s and t, return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t (counting duplicates). If none exists, return the empty string "".

The tests are built so the shortest window is unique.
problems.hint: Expand right until the window covers t (track how many required characters are still missing). Then shrink from the left as much as possible, recording the best window.

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.description: A window of size k slides over nums from left to right, one step at a time. Return an array with the maximum of each window position.
problems.hint: Keep a deque of indices whose values are in decreasing order. Drop indices that left the window from the front, and smaller values from the back before pushing.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.description: heights describes a histogram whose bars are all 1 unit wide. Return the area of the largest rectangle that fits entirely inside the histogram.
problems.hint: For each bar, the widest rectangle of its height extends until the first shorter bar on each side. A stack of increasing heights finds those boundaries in one pass.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.description:
Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2, return the median of all their values combined. (With an even total count, the median is the average of the two middle values.)

The target complexity is O(log(m + n)), though a linear merge will also pass these tests.
problems.hint: Binary search a cut in the smaller array so that the left parts of both arrays together contain half of the values and every left value ≤ every right value.

problems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
problems.description:
You get an array of k linked lists, each sorted ascending. Merge them all into one sorted list and return its head.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: A min-heap (PriorityQueue) holding the current head of each list always gives you the next smallest node in O(log k).

problems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
problems.description:
Reverse the nodes of the list k at a time and return the new head. If the number of nodes left at the end is less than k, leave them in their original order.

Only change links, not node values.

Lists are shown as arrays of node values, from head to tail.
problems.hint: Process groups one at a time: check that k nodes remain, reverse exactly those k, and connect the previous group's tail to the new group's head.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.description:
A path is a sequence of nodes where each pair of neighbours is connected by an edge; each node appears at most once, and the path doesn't need to pass through the root. Its sum is the sum of its node values.

Return the maximum sum of any non-empty path.

Trees are shown in level order (row by row, left to right), with null marking a missing child.
problems.hint: For each node compute the best downward path starting at it (ignore negative branches with max(0, …)). The best path that 'bends' at the node is node + leftGain + rightGain.

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.description:
Given an m × n grid of letters board and a list of words, return every word that can be traced on the board. A word is traced by moving between horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, and a single cell can't be used twice in the same word.

Return each found word once, in any order.
problems.hint: Put all words in a trie, then DFS from each cell while walking the trie at the same time — one search finds many words. Remove a word from the trie once found.

problems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.description:
Implement class MedianFinder:

  • MedianFinder() starts empty
  • void addNum(int num) adds a number
  • double findMedian() returns the median of everything added so far (the average of the two middle values when the count is even)

findMedian is only called after at least one number was added. Answers within 10⁻⁵ are accepted.

Tests list the calls made and the value each one returns (null for void methods).
problems.hint: Keep two heaps: a max-heap with the smaller half and a min-heap with the larger half, balanced so their sizes differ by at most one.

problems.title: N-Queens
problems.description:
Place n chess queens on an n × n board so that no two attack each other (no shared row, column or diagonal). Return every distinct solution.

Each solution is a list of n strings, one per row, where 'Q' is a queen and '.' an empty square. Solutions may be in any order.
problems.hint: Place one queen per row. Track used columns and both diagonal directions (row − col and row + col) in sets or boolean arrays.

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.description:
A transformation sequence goes from beginWord to endWord changing exactly one letter at each step, where every intermediate word (and endWord) must be in wordList.

Return the number of words in the shortest such sequence (including both ends), or 0 if none exists.
constraints: All words have the same length, lowercase
problems.hint: BFS over words, where neighbours differ by one letter. Generate neighbours by trying all 26 letters at each position and checking a HashSet of the word list.

problems.title: Distinct Subsequences
problems.description:
Count the number of distinct ways to pick characters from s (keeping their order) so that they spell t. Two ways are different if they use a different set of positions in s.

The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = ways to form t's first j chars from s's first i chars. Always inherit dp[i−1][j]; if s[i−1] == t[j−1], also add dp[i−1][j−1]. dp[i][0] = 1.
